scope: Native stage message/pause declarations and corrected partial graph-callback matrix layout; all shared-header consumers verified.
changes: Add static UpdateMessage and PS_Init declarations to the existing dScStage_c header. Their definitions use the genuine scene declaration; UpdateMessage also uses Message.h instead of a local class stand-in.

PS_Init names the main/sub enabled-layer masks and blend targets, and retains numeric unknown pause-state decisions. Its raw scalar SetBlendBrightness interface is explicitly documented because the typed u16 call adds four narrowing instructions.
GraphCallback2 replaces a two-word Matrix2x2 definition with the four-word record consumed by G2x::SetBGyAffine. Name the matrix, origin and target coordinates in an explicitly partial callback view.
Retain the legacy GraphCallback2 method symbol/scope and state that dispatchers pass the graph callback object as this. This is not a complete callback class or original-TU reconstruction.
Remove obsolete local-shadow and double-mangling comments from the changed sources, while preserving the actual linkage/receiver constraints.

evidence.static_methods: UpdateMessage and PS_Init use no scene instance state and were already defined as static members of their local stand-in classes. Their existing public symbols remain identical; real header declarations emit no new vtable/key-function ownership.
evidence.matrix: src/engine/gx/G2x.cpp defines Matrix2x2 as int m[4], reads four20.12 entries and computes dx=c-a,dy=d-b before applying the affine transform. This supports the four-entry local matrix and originX/Y,targetX/Y names. Callback matrix begins+4 after its vptr.
evidence.callback_receiver: notes/scene-provenance.md documents graph callback vtable slots1/2 and dispatchers passing the callback object in r0 without another argument. The source keeps this explicit legacy-scope limitation and does not reinterpret it as the full playable-scene layout.
evidence.pause_blend: The typed G2x::SetBlendBrightness call inserts lsl/lsr pairs narrowing each target mask to16bits. Retaining the original scalar extern preserves the direct ROM call and all emitted bytes. No unresolved-slot claim is hidden by that choice.
